entries.proposition: For early-infantile DEE (the syndrome class in which most WWOX-DEE patients are classified) the evidence for ketogenic therapy is small case series and reports; responsive etiologies named are ALG13, SCN2A, KCNQ2, mitochondrial respiratory-chain disorders, creatine transporter deficiency and glycine encephalopathy. Class level, not WWOX evidence.
entries.snippet: Evidence supporting KDT in EIDEE is limited primarily to small case series and individual case reports

experimental_context.system: narrative review of ketogenic dietary therapy in DEE syndromes and genes (class level; NOT WWOX evidence)

entries.proposition: For epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures, 25 of 40 KCNT1 patients with reported outcomes (62.5 percent) showed some benefit, mostly described qualitatively and started at about one year of age; class level, not WWOX evidence.
entries.snippet: Among the 40 patients for whom outcomes were available, 25 (62.5%) showed some degree of benefit, although responses were frequently described qualitatively rather than using standardized seizure-reduction thresholds

experimental_context.system: narrative review of ketogenic dietary therapy in DEE syndromes and genes (class level; NOT WWOX evidence)

entries.proposition: Gene-level KD responders in a meta-analysis (overall 58 percent of 849 patients): SLC2A1 96 percent, SCN2A 73, SCN1A 64, STXBP1 54, KCNQ2 42, KCNT1 24, CDKL5 23, SCN8A 15; seizure freedom overall 29 percent. WWOX is not among the genes. Class level.
entries.snippet: A meta-analysis reported gene-specific responder rates (an overall rate of 58% among 849 patients) of 96% for SLC2A1 (n = 87), 73% for SCN2A (n = 16)

entries.proposition: Gene-specific use is described as nonspecific, broad-acting antiseizure therapy generally after failure of two or more ASMs and supported mainly by case series and small cohorts; transporter-related disorders did best and genes of structural integrity or homeostatic regulation did worst in one cohort. Class level.
